hyps.why: Stepping down from a divergent or unstable learning rate (0.0774 and above) recovers a lot of accuracy, while the same step at mid or low rates has little effect.
At 1e-5 to 1.3e-4 the network is undertrained within 243 epochs, so a higher rate helps much more than it does elsewhere.
Raising an already large Adam rate pushes training into divergence or chance-level accuracy.
With a tiny learning rate, a larger batch means fewer updates in 243 epochs, which worsens underfitting.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, which stabilizes training at high learning rates.
Small batches combined with large learning rates give very noisy, unstable updates.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to divergence and dead units at high learning rates.
Wider layers produce larger effective updates, which makes high learning rates more unstable.
Strong L2 at 0.129 to 1 causes underfitting, whereas small alpha values barely change accuracy.
Adding capacity helps most when the layers are narrow (16 to 40 units), with diminishing returns at larger widths.
